docs: Scenario table for scripts/fake-openai.mjs. Data only: add a scripted case here instead of editing the server.
A scenario is one of three kinds:
kind=chat  -> 200, scripted `chunks`. In `stream:true` mode each chunk becomes one `data:` SSE frame; in
`stream:false` mode the deltas are folded into one OpenAI message. A chunk carrying `usage`
emits the OpenAI include_usage final chunk (choices:[]).
kind=error -> the HTTP status in `status` (default 500) plus the OpenAI-style `error` body.
kind=hang  -> the request is accepted and never answered (timeout / fail-closed tests). No timer is
created, and the socket is destroyed by close().
A `chat` delta is verbatim OpenAI Chat Completions: {role}, {content}, {tool_calls:[{index,type,function:{name,arguments}}]}.
`function.arguments` is ALWAYS a JSON string (never an object).
Tool-call ids are generated per request as `call_fake_<seq>_<index>` unless a chunk pins `id`.
Optional `followUp: <name>`: a chat scenario is only served while the request history carries NO `role:tool`
message; once a tool result is present the followUp scenario answers instead. This keeps a scripted tool-call
turn from looping forever (the model would otherwise keep re-asking for the same call) and stays deterministic:
the branch is a pure function of the request history. `scenario_served` in the request log shows the branch.
Override any scenario per request with a trigger token in the last user message: [[scenario:NAME]].

text.description: Plain assistant text: role delta, two content deltas, finish_reason=stop.

tool-call-bash.description: One tool_calls delta invoking bash with a destructive command (balanced preset should deny via tags/chain).

tool-call-three-parallel.description: Three tool_calls in one response (bash + web_fetch + todo_write), one delta per call, indices 0-2.

code-mode.description: call run_code and, inside the program, dispatch a denied shell tool. Uses `tools.pwsh` because this host is Windows (bash-sandbox is disabled there); the plugin denies pwsh by name, so the sub-dispatch must still surface as tool_denied.
code-mode.note: The task brief assumed {"code":"await bash({command:'echo hi'})"}. The real dsh-tools schema requires `description` too and mounts every tool under the `tools` global, so the scripted program uses await tools.pwsh(...). On 0.2.2-rc.1 Code Mode is the PTC tool executor, not a tools.mode value.

function.name: run_code
function.arguments: {"code":"await tools.pwsh({ command: 'echo hi', description: 'echo hi' })\nreturn 'ok'","description":"Echo hi through the shell tool in code mode"}

error-500.description: HTTP 500 with an OpenAI-style error body (no stream).

hang.description: Accept the request and never respond, for timeout / fail-closed tests. close() destroys the socket.

judge-allow.description: The safeharness semantic judge's verdict: allow. Served only when the request's last user message carries the [safeharness-judge] marker (table.judgeScenario/judgeTrigger).

judge-block.description: The safeharness semantic judge's verdict: block. Use with --judge-scenario judge-block to prove enforce-buffer replaces the answer.

tool-call-patrol.description: Call the plugin's read-only safeharness_patrol tool, then finish with text once the tool result exists.

usage.description: Plain text reply plus an OpenAI include_usage final chunk and a finish_reason.
